metadata.note: Yes -- Watertown, NY had passenger rail starting 1851. The Watertown and Rome Railroad (chartered 1832, but construction languished for 15 years) finally reached Watertown on September 5, 1851 -- 'the first engine reached Watertown...at eleven o'clock in the night', per a contemporary account. The line was extended to Cape Vincent on Lake Ontario/the St. Lawrence River in 1852, with regular service beginning May 1 1852 -- this was the original northern terminus. The company later merged (1861) with a separate line building toward Ogdensburg to form the Rome, Watertown and Ogdensburg Railroad (RW&O), which by 1862 also reached Ogdensburg via a branch from De Kalb Junction, and eventually extended through Potsdam and Norwood to Massena. RW&O was leased to the New York Central & Hudson River Railroad in 1891 and fully merged into the New York Central in 1913, becoming its 'St. Lawrence Division'. Geometry is real-traced from OpenStreetMap for most of both routes (combining active rail with abandoned-railway tagging, since much of this rural branch network is no longer in active service) -- one ~26km gap remains (Lacona to Adams, via Mannsville and Pierrepont Manor) where neither active nor abandoned rail tagging exists in OSM, shown as a straight-line approximation between the real, correctly-ordered station towns. EXTENSION ADDED: the full RW&O namesake network now includes the Watertown-Massena main line (via Evans Mills, Philadelphia, Antwerp, Gouverneur, Richville, De Kalb Junction, Canton, Potsdam, and Norwood) and the De Kalb Junction-Ogdensburg branch that gave the railroad its name. Geometry: Watertown-Evans Mills-Philadelphia (25.7km) and Canton-Potsdam-Norwood-Massena (44.8km) are real-traced from OpenStreetMap (active rail combined with abandoned-railway tagging). The middle stretch (Philadelphia through Antwerp, Gouverneur, Richville, to De Kalb Junction, ~66km) and the entire De Kalb Junction-Ogdensburg branch could not be matched to any connected rail geometry in OSM -- confirmed disconnected across three independent tracing attempts with different data pulls -- and are straight-line approximations between the real, correctly-ordered station towns from the source guide. COLOR SPLIT 2026-08-24: per the same-company-same-color rule, feature(s) whose ownership passed to the New York Central were split at the documented transfer date into a pre-NYC feature (original company color) and an NYC-colored feature (matching new_york_central.geojson's canonical color), sharing identical geometry, rather than coloring the whole multi-era line with the original company's color throughout.

metadata.rome_terminal_note: Rome end retraced Aug 2026. The line's Rome terminus is the junction with the New York Central main line in downtown Rome (-75.46103, 43.20891); from there the RW&O ran northwest via Ridge Mills, Lee Center and Camden. Until the NYC realigned its main line and rebuilt Rome station south of the city in 1912-14, that main line ran through the city centre, so Watertown trains reached the downtown depot at this junction; after 1914 the branch reached the relocated station by a new south leg (the NYC 'Rome Branch') dropping from 43.2179,-75.4803 to the main line west of town, not traced here. An earlier version of this file started at a Rome city-centre point and then ran south down the abandoned Rome & Clinton branch (a New York, Ontario & Western line, built 1871, abandoned 1932) before jumping back north -- that was a tracing error, not history.
metadata.oswego_branch_note: Oswego & Rome branch added 2026-08-24: Oswego - Mexico - Richland, 46.0 km (28.6 miles), joining the Rome - Watertown main line at Richland (the two features share that vertex exactly). It is carried as two features so the change of ownership is visible on the map rather than only in these notes: 'or-oswego-richland' covers the Oswego & Rome and RW&O years 1866-1913, and 'or-oswego-richland-nyc' picks it up in New York Central house colour (#5C677D) with segments for the March 14 1891 NYC&HR lease and the April 1913 consolidation, matching how the other RW&O features in this file are split. Sources disagree on the exact April 1913 day (April 12 and April 16 both appear), so only the month is stated.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
